Which advertiser x market pairs are off.text:
For 2026-Q3, Contoso Mobility in Spain overshot plan by 12%, triggering a 50% make-good credit on excess media value. Fabrikam Beauty in Italy under-delivered by 8%, incurring a 2% net media budget penalty. Adventure Works Travel's variances stayed below 5%, so no compensation applies. Northwind Foods' quarterly fluctuations do not yield credits or penalties, as delivery is assessed annually. Litware Retail's contract disallows compensation or penalties regardless of variance.

Key figures: Contoso Mobility Spain 286M planned, 321M delivered (12% over), Fabrikam Beauty Italy 140M planned, 129M delivered (-8%).

What is the gap between what was spent a.text:
The billing gap shows spend exceeding billed amounts, notably in Litware Retail UK with a €731,282 gap. Across all advertisers and markets, there are several campaigns affected, for example, 4 for Adventure Works Travel UK, but zero missing billing invoice rows at invoice grain. Across the five indexed master agreement.text:
The five master agreements differ in delivery variance regimes: Advertiser A in the UK with Media Owner X offers automatic compensation beyond 3% under-delivery (Article 6.3), plus a 50% credit for over-delivery beyond 10% (Article 6.2), both without client request. Advertiser B in France with Media Owner Y excludes compensation for up to 5% under-delivery and penalties only apply beyond that (Articles 5.1, 6.1, 6.4). Advertiser C in Germany with Media Owner Z imposes agency penalties beyond 5% shortfall (Article 6.2), plus compensation past 10% (Articles 6.3-6.4). Others exclude compensation or penalty regardless of variance (Article 6.1).

### SOURCE
ZM-ADV-001-2026 Articles 6.2, 6.3, 6.4
ZM-ADV-005-2026 Articles 5.1, 6.1, 6.4
ZM-ADV-002-2026 Articles 6.2, 6.3, 6.4
ZM-ADV-004-2026 Article 6.1

Compare 2026-Q2 and 2026-Q3 for the same.text:
Quarterly delivery variances flipped sign in several advertiser-market pairs this Q3; none are newly introduced pairs. Notably, Adventure Works Travel France shifted from 0.7% over-delivery to 1.7% under; Contoso Mobility Germany moved from 1.3% under to 0.6% over; Fabrikam Beauty Spain changed from 0.3% over to 1.1% under. Contracts for most advertisers mandate delivery variance assessment by quarter, making these figures contractually relevant. Northwind Foods alone assesses variance annually, so their Q3 over-delivery of 0.3% in Spain is not yet a contractual event.

### SOURCE  
Planned Impressions, Delivered Impressions, Delivery vs Plan % by advertiser_name, market_name, quarter

For the advertisers carrying the billing.text:
Adventure Works Travel, Contoso Mobility, Fabrikam Beauty, and Northwind Foods have contracts ensuring 100% rebate pass-through without specific rate or threshold, consistent with a 2.5% rebate applied on gross billed. Their combined net net billed is about €59.7M. Litware Retail has a 50/50 rebate sharing clause, but the full 2.5% rebate was applied, benefiting Litware by roughly €280K on €9.6M net billed. This is the only discrepancy between applied and contractual rebate terms.

### SOURCE  
Gross Billed, Rebate Amount, Rebate % of Gross, Net Net Billed by advertiser with billing gaps

Across the five indexed master agreement.text:
Among the five indexed master agreements, the most restrictive claim window for delivery variance or invoiced omissions is 90 days post the broadcast month, set by Microsoft US with Zava (Article 9.2). Google UK with Annexe allows up to 120 days, while Amazon Germany and Meta France set 90 days. TikTok Australia lacks explicit terms in the corpus. None specify a 15-day notice period. Microsoft US with Zava thus enforces the shortest invoicing claim period, emphasizing timely claims after delivery.

### SOURCE
ZM-ADV-001-2026 Article 9.2  
ZM-ADV-004-2026 Article 9.2  
ZM-ADV-003-2026 Article 9.2  
ZM-ADV-002-2026 Article 9.2

For Contoso Mobility, follow Advertiser.text:
Contoso Mobility ran campaigns with the brands Contoso EV and Contoso Fleet across Germany, Spain, France, Italy, and the UK, all of which are explicitly covered in the master agreement. Delivery closely matched plan with Contoso EV Germany delivering 119.6M of 120.9M planned impressions (99%), Contoso Fleet Spain delivering 185.2M of 181.8M planned (102%), and Contoso Fleet Italy delivering 16.9M of 16.8M planned (101%). No brands or markets ran beyond covered scope, confirming full contract compliance.

Clause: Master Agreement Article 3 — Scope, ZM-ADV-001-2026

Markets: Germany, Spain, France, Italy, United Kingdom

Take the delivery variances observed in.text:
In 2026-Q3, only three advertisers triggered clauses in their master agreements based on delivery variances:

Contoso Mobility in Spain over-delivered by 12.0% (planned 286M, delivered 321M), triggering a compensation credit to the client.

Fabrikam Beauty in Italy under-delivered by 8.0% (planned 140M, delivered 129M), triggering a penalty owed by the agency.

Adventure Works Travel’s small under-deliveries (below 5%) and Northwind Foods’ quarterly variances do not trigger penalties or credits.

Litware Retail’s UK +11.0% over-delivery does not generate compensation per contract terms.

Agency owes client Fabrikam Italy penalties; client benefits from Contoso Spain make-good.

dimensions: dim_advertiser[advertiser_name], dim_market[market_name]

Give the state of the portfolio over the.text:
Across the portfolio, we are exactly on our investment plan; the only real risk is concentrated in a very small number of under‑delivering campaigns, not at advertiser or market level. The focus is to work those specific cases through with the relevant media owners, not to reopen budgets.

We have 80 campaigns in total, with 40 still live. We planned €61.5 M and have spent €61.5 M, i.e. 100.0% budget consumption overall, with 4 campaigns over‑delivering and 2 under‑delivering on impressions.

Give [Total Invoices] and [Net Billed (E.text:
All five advertisers have significant outstanding invoices, with oldest unsettled invoices ranging from 81 to 112 days. According to their contracts, Adventure Works Travel and Fabrikam Beauty must pay within 30 days end of month, Contoso Mobility and Northwind Foods have 45 days, and Litware Retail has 60 days. As a result, invoices from Adventure Works Travel, Contoso Mobility, Fabrikam Beauty, and Litware Retail are past due, while Northwind Foods' outstanding invoices, oldest at 81 days, remain inside its payment window.

Break the billing gap down by dim_media_.text:
The billing gap is concentrated with a small set of digital and audio partners in late Q3, and in almost every case it’s one missing or late invoice per owner‑month, not a cloud of tiny errors. This is a publisher‑billing follow‑up, not a systemic overspend issue.

Worst case is Halcyon Social in September: about €2.76 M spent vs €2.54 M billed (≈‑€0.30 M gap), coming from a single invoice. Similar, but smaller, one‑off gaps appear with Kestrel Retail Media, Alpine Digital and Solstice Audio in September.

Which advertisers and which markets conc.text:
Spend is highly concentrated in a handful of big advertiser–market pairs, and the delivery and billing risks we saw earlier largely sit inside that core, not on the long tail. That means any issue with, say, UK retail or German food has portfolio‑level impact, so we manage those relationships very actively.

Roughly, Adventure Works in the UK, Northwind in Germany, Litware in the UK and Contoso in Spain together represent a bit over a third of total net spend, all running around 99–101% budget consumption.

Compare the two sources for the same cam.text:
The live stream and the batch view are broadly pointing the same way: campaigns that are ahead of plan on the full‑campaign numbers are also pushing volume through the live window, and under‑ or near‑plan campaigns show more modest live volumes. But they do not cover the same period and must not be compared as if they did.

Example: the Contoso EV Spain campaign shows 199.9 M planned vs 223.9 M delivered (+12.0%) in the batch model, while the stream only captures 16.2 M impressions over 27 Aug–3 Sep, i.e. a short slice of that delivery.

### SOURCE
RT_Zava_Media (Eventhouse)  
Table: pacing_events, grouped by campaign_id  
Field: sum(impressions_delta), min/max(timestamp) for CMP‑0041…CMP‑0080  
SM_Zava_Media (Semantic Model)  
Group: dim_campaign[campaign_id] for CMP‑0041…CMP‑0080  
Measures: [Planned Impressions], [Delivered Impressions], [Delivery vs Plan %]

What is the pacing stream reporting? Fro.text:
Live, the stream shows a small group of campaigns running slightly hot, all within a controlled band and consistent with the batch view: good momentum, not a runaway spend issue. The window we see is about a week, so this is a short‑term pulse, not the whole story.

Examples: Contoso EV Spain is at 199.9 M planned vs 223.9 M delivered (+12.0%); Contoso Fleet Spain, 86.5 M vs 96.9 M (+12.0%); Litware Fashion UK, 165.6 M vs 183.8 M (+11.0%). These are the main over‑consuming campaigns in the live stream.

### SOURCE
RT_Zava_Media (Eventhouse)  
Table: pacing_events, summarize by campaign_id → avg(pacing_index), sum(impressions_delta), sum(spend_delta), min/max(timestamp); filter avg_pacing_index > 1  
SM_Zava_Media (Semantic Model)  
Group: dim_campaign[campaign_id] for those campaigns  
Measures: [Planned Impressions], [Delivered Impressions], [Delivery vs Plan %]

From the pacing_events table in the Even.text:
Live, the stream shows a handful of campaigns running comfortably above 1 on pacing for the whole week‑long window, but with fairly flat hourly profiles: over‑consuming in a controlled way rather than accelerating. It’s a signal to watch, not an alarm.

The window we see runs roughly from 27 August to 3 September (UTC). For example, the Contoso EV Spain campaign sits around 1.10–1.20 most hours over that week and, at campaign level, is 199.9 M planned vs 223.9 M delivered (+12.0%), fully consistent with that live pattern.

### SOURCE
RT_Zava_Media (Eventhouse)  
Table: pacing_events  
KQL #1: summarize avg(pacing_index) by campaign_id, bin(timestamp, 1h) ordered by campaign_id, hour_bucket  
KQL #2: where pacing_index > 1 summarize min(timestamp), max(timestamp), max(pacing_index) by campaign_id  
SM_Zava_Media (Semantic Model)  
Group: dim_campaign[campaign_id] for over‑consuming campaigns; measures [Planned Impressions], [Delivered Impressions], [Delivery vs Plan %]
